tasks.short: Maintain time, wage, receipt and inspection reports

steps.what: Collect and enter employee time, wage references, receipts and inspection results
outputs: dated source entries with employee or job identifiers

steps.what: Compare work records with roster, rate and receipt references
inputs: dated source entries with employee or job identifiers
outputs: draft comparison results with unmatched entries

steps.what: Investigate discrepancies and correct the underlying work records
inputs: draft comparison results with unmatched entries

steps.what: Prepare the work report from verified values and explanations
Check and send the final report to its authorised internal recipient

tasks.design: Reuse native time records in {HCM} and operational records in {OPS_SYSTEM}, with a deterministic comparison and existing report layout. The supervisor captures missing information, resolves differences and checks the exact report sent through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate source records force repeated reference checks and report transcription.
tasks.enabler_now: Native time records and operational views can share stable employee and job identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: A mismatch does not establish which underlying observation is correct.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor checks the facts with staff and explains irregular work.
tasks.altitude: Maintain records with fewer repeated comparisons and copied totals.

evidence.claim: Logistics workforce software supports time and attendance records; the digest does not establish automatic inspection or receipt capture.
Comparison and report savings are unmeasured local estimates.

assumptions: Existing work reports are read by operations administration; the task includes source capture, corrections, report writing and an actual internal send.

Employees produce time declarations, payroll administration produces approved rates, receipt issuers produce receipt documents and inspectors produce observations in existing duties. The supervisor selects identifiers, period, rates and receipt references and enters missing inspection results in s1; 27 hours of this capture work remain. No free structured inspection flag is assumed.
The routine compares only captured identifiers and numerical fields; missing references return to retained s3 manual investigation. No wage payment, payroll posting or automatic alert is proposed.

Native field defaults remove three of30 capture hours, the comparison removes20 manual check hours, and the layout removes10 of25 report hours. Different operations support each estimate; explanation writing and ordinary same-system saves remain.
Any employee-monitoring access changes require the organisation's applicable governance before rollout.
unknowns: Whether reports already use native totals
research_questions: Can each report value be traced to a captured source without extra supervisor data entry?

already_counted.description: Source selection and entry in s1 and discrepancy resolution in s3 remain.

incremental.description: Supervisor maintains comparison exceptions after rate or roster changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact report period, employee/job scope, figures, explanations and recipient checked before the real send; subsequent edits invalidate the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R67, gross33 minus focal upkeep2 gives net31. Low15 retains all30 capture hours, eight manual comparison hours and20 report hours alongside20 investigation and5 send hours: R83, less2 upkeep. High25 retains28 capture, four comparison and16 report hours plus25 investigation/send: R73, less2 upkeep. The conservative cases reflect incompatible identifiers and report layouts, not a shared percentage discount.

steps.what: Retrieve the current work orders and check their release status
Prepare the work order briefing with locations, sequence and handling precautions
Check and transmit the final work orders to the assigned laborers
Explain the work order sequence and precautions to laborers
Check understanding and resolve questions before the work starts

tasks.design: Configure a current-order view and reusable briefing layout in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The supervisor supplies local precautions, transmits the checked order through {CHAT} and explains it in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervisors may search for released orders and retype stable order details into a briefing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and layouts can reuse the order's existing identifiers and locations.
tasks.still_hard: Worker questions and changing floor conditions are not solved by a formatted order.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor establishes that the team understands the work.
tasks.altitude: Prepare a clearer briefing with less copying.

evidence.claim: A native order view and reusable briefing layout can reduce navigation and copying; the size of the benefit here is unmeasured.

assumptions: The existing briefing is the order text actually transmitted to laborers, not a newly invented meeting record. Explaining and checking understanding remain separate.

The planner produces released order identifiers, locations and quantities through existing order release. The supervisor validates release and assignment in s1, captures local precautions in s2 and manually resolves missing fields; all associated capture time is retained within those steps.

A native order filter removes three of15 search hours; the briefing layout removes five of20 copying hours but none of the local safety assessment. No automated send or extra acknowledgement log is added.
Crew allocation is handled in the schedule task. This task prices the order-specific briefing and transmission, not a second copy of the roster communication.
unknowns: Whether work orders already provide a usable briefing layout
research_questions: Which briefing fields are currently retyped rather than displayed directly?

already_counted.description: Order validation and local briefing preparation remain in s1 and s2.

incremental.description: Supervisor updates briefing layout when order fields change.

approvals.approved_version: Exact order revision, job scope, local precautions and assigned recipients checked immediately before transmission; any change invalidates the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R92, gross8 less focal upkeep1 gives net7. Low0 retains all100 hours when the native order already serves as the briefing and no configuration is adopted. High5 retains13 search hours and16 briefing hours, with all65 transmission/explanation/understanding hours, giving R94 and net5 after upkeep1. Central retains12 search and15 briefing hours.

tasks.short: Plan schedules and assign duties under fluctuating workloads

steps.what: Gather current workloads, available staff and qualification constraints
Choose duty assignments and schedule changes for the workload
Write the work schedules and assigned duties in the roster
Check and communicate the final roster changes to affected staff
Monitor staffing adequacy as the workload changes

tasks.design: Use native availability views in {HCM}, the work queue in {OPS_SYSTEM} and a reusable shift pattern to record the supervisor's assignments. The supervisor chooses allocations and checks the specific roster communicated through {CHAT}; no automated personnel allocation or performance scoring is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checking availability and rewriting repeated shift cells can consume scheduling time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native roster views and reusable shift patterns separate clerical work from assignment judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Absence, urgent work and safe combinations of staff can change during a shift.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor balances local capability, fairness and workload.

ambition.what: Revisit staffing when the work queue changes without rebuilding the whole roster.

tasks.altitude: Retain staffing decisions while reducing schedule transcription.

reach.learn: Which fluctuations require actual staffing changes

evidence.claim: Logistics workforce software supports scheduling, forecasting and time and attendance; this design uses native roster functions without delegating assignment decisions.
The retained scheduling time and proposed savings are local estimates.

assumptions: The task includes context gathering, assignment decisions, actual roster writing, communication and monitoring. Order-specific instructions are priced in the separate work-order task.

The planner produces work-queue quantities, staff declare availability and personnel administration maintains qualification references in existing processes. The supervisor validates these in s1; missing or outdated information requires manual contact within its17 retained hours. No cost-free readiness flag is assumed.

The native availability view removes three of20 navigation hours. Reusing a shift pattern removes10.5 of30 roster rewriting hours while preserving changes, conflict checks and ordinary author saves without self-approval.
No machine allocation, alert or automatic roster distribution is implied. The real communication is its own retained gated step.
unknowns: How often shifts resemble reusable patterns
research_questions: How much roster entry survives after a pattern is copied for a volatile shift?

already_counted.description: Staffing context validation and roster correction remain in s1 and s3.

incremental.description: Supervisor maintains reusable patterns and checks changed availability definitions.

approvals.approved_version: Exact dated roster, individual duties, shift times and affected recipients checked before communication; edits invalidate the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R86.5, gross13.5 less upkeep2 gives net11.5. Low3 retains all20 context hours and25 roster hours because changing duties require most cells rewritten, plus50 decision/communication/monitoring hours: R95, net3. High8 retains19 context hours and21 roster hours for partly reusable shifts plus50 other hours: R90, net8. Central retains17 context and19.5 roster hours with compatible patterns.

tasks.short: Review credentials, interview and recommend hiring decisions

steps.what: Review candidate credentials against the vacancy requirements
Conduct the interview and clarify the candidate's relevant experience
Write interview evidence in the existing hiring evaluation form
Make the hiring decision or recommendation from the reviewed evidence
Check and send the final recommendation to the hiring team

tasks.design: Configure the application view and existing evaluation form in {ATS} to put vacancy criteria beside the original evidence. The supervisor interviews, writes evidence and decides personally, then checks the recommendation sent through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Application navigation and repeatedly setting up evaluation headings add clerical work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recruitment views and reusable forms can remove that setup without scoring candidates.
tasks.still_hard: Credentials and interview answers need context-sensitive assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor probes experience and owns the reasoned recommendation.
tasks.altitude: Reduce evaluation form setup while preserving evidence gathering and hiring judgement.

reach.learn: Which vacancy requirements need clearer interview questions

evidence.claim: Native application views and reusable evaluation forms can reduce clerical setup; this is an unmeasured design without automated hiring recommendations.

assumptions: An existing written evaluation and internal recommendation are part of the current hiring process and are read by the hiring team; no new interview transcript or trailing activity log is added.

Candidates produce applications and credential documents, and recruiters maintain vacancy requirements. The supervisor checks those originals in s1 and produces interview evidence in s2 and its structured written record in s3; all evidence capture and assessment time is counted.

The application view removes2.5 of25 navigation hours. Reusable form headings remove three of15 writing hours; writing actual answers, checking accuracy and ordinary author saves remain. There is no transcription model, ranking or automatic decision.
The internal send gate applies to the version circulated, not to saving the author's evaluation form.
unknowns: Whether the current evaluation form already includes vacancy-specific headings
research_questions: Do reusable headings remove setup time without reducing the specificity of interview evidence?

already_counted.description: Credential review, interviewing, evidence writing and judgement remain in s1 through s4.

incremental.description: Supervisor updates form headings when vacancy requirements change.

approvals.approved_version: Actual interview question or statement checked for relevance to the vacancy before speaking; new questions need a fresh check.
Exact recommendation, rationale, candidate identifier, attachments and hiring-team recipients checked immediately before sending; changes invalidate the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R94.5, gross5.5 less focal upkeep0.5 gives net5. Low0 retains all work where the existing ATS already presents criteria and form headings and no configuration is adopted. High3.5 retains24 credential-review hours and12 form-writing hours plus60 interview/decision/send hours: R96, less0.5 upkeep. Central retains22.5 review and12 form hours when the view also removes repeated document navigation.

role.altitude: Keep operational and personnel judgement with the supervisor while reducing record comparison and repeated writing.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who keeps clear operational records and usable instructions while staying close to the work and the team.
